description: What one pinned account's status icon shows: exactly one content value plus the flag outdated, from the account's headline presentation, that reading's validity and whether the account needs signing in again. No strings, no pixels. Rule, decided in this order: (1) error when the account needs signing in again, or when the validity is error, with or without a headline. A partial result with a usable headline is not an error: its caller passes the validity the reading has (current, stale or reset due), never error. (2) exhausted when the headline is exhausted, in either display mode, whatever its token. (3) unknown (drawn as a dash) when there is no headline, or its token is the unknown token. (4) none (the glyph alone) when the token is 100. (5) figure with a number 0 to 99 otherwise: the token >99 becomes 99 and <1 becomes 0, every other token is its own whole number. outdated (drawn as an underline) is true when the validity is stale or reset due and the content is figure or none; it is false for error, exhausted and unknown. The icon's number is deliberately lossy, so anything spoken or written in words uses the presentation's token, never this number. The validity is passed explicitly and never inferred from the token or the exhausted flag. Expected values are written by hand from this rule, not generated from either implementation. Both platforms read this file unchanged with a strict decoder: an unknown or missing key fails the suite.
schema: vectors: array of { name: string (unique, says what the case proves); headline: null when the account has no usage window, otherwise { token: string, one of a whole number 0 to 100 written without sign or leading zero, "<1", ">99", or "\u2014" (the unknown token); side: "left" | "used" (the display mode the token counts); exhausted: boolean (the provider's verdict carried by the presentation) }; validity: "current" | "stale" | "resetDue" | "error"; needsReauthentication: boolean; expected: { content: "error" | "exhausted" | "unknown" | "none" | "figure"; figure: integer 0 to 99 when content is "figure", otherwise null; outdated: boolean } }.

vectors.name: a current figure in Left is its number
a current figure in Used is its number
a single digit stays a single digit
a single digit in Used stays a single digit
nothing used is 0 and not exhausted
under one percent becomes 0
under one percent used becomes 0
over ninety-nine left becomes 99
over ninety-nine used becomes 99
99 is still a figure
a full allowance shows the glyph alone
an exhausted window in Left is exhausted, not 0
an exhausted window in Used is exhausted, not the glyph alone
an exhausted window without a numeric figure is exhausted, not a dash
an exhausted window that still reports a figure is exhausted
no headline is unknown
a headline without a figure is unknown
needing to sign in again outranks a figure
needing to sign in again outranks exhausted
needing to sign in again outranks unknown
needing to sign in again without a headline is an error
a failed reading with a headline is an error, not its old number
a failed reading without a headline is an error
a failed reading outranks exhausted
a partial result with a usable headline arrives as current and shows its figure
a stale figure keeps its number, underlined
a reset-due figure in Used keeps its number, underlined
a stale reading under one percent is an underlined 0
a stale full allowance underlines the lone glyph
a reset-due full allowance underlines the lone glyph
a stale exhausted window is exhausted without an underline
a reset-due exhausted window in Used is exhausted without an underline
a stale account without a headline is unknown without an underline
a reset-due headline without a figure is unknown without an underline
a stale account that needs signing in again is an error without an underline
